Attention, Explained

This page contains inline mathematics, which extraction pipelines render either as MathML, as the original LaTeX source, or as mangled plain text. Each of those is a different markdown shape and a dependency bump can move between them without any test in the repository noticing.

The attention function is defined as \( \mathrm{softmax}(QK^{\top}/\sqrt{d_k})V \) where \(d_k\) is the key dimension.

Derivation

Expanding the definition gives the following, which is displayed as a block equation on the page and must not vanish entirely during conversion:

\[ \mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V) = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V \]

After the equation the prose continues, because a converter that treats math as the end of the article would lose the rest of the page, and that is the regression this fixture is here to catch.

Implementation notes

The reference implementation keeps the numerically unstable term out:

def attention(q, k, v):
    scores = q @ k.T / math.sqrt(d_k)
    return softmax(scores) @ v

Final paragraph with a reference so the tail of the document still contains structure.
